# Psalm 41 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the music director. A psalm of David.

**2** How blessed are those who are concerned for the poor! The LORD will deliver them in times of trouble.

**3** The LORD protects them and keeps them alive. He gives them prosperity in the land and rescues them from their enemies.

**4** The LORD nurses them when they are sick and restores them to health.

**5** I said, 'LORD, have mercy on me. Heal me, for I have sinned against You.'

**6** But my enemies say nothing but evil about me. 'When will he finally die and be forgotten?' they ask.

**7** They visit me as if they were my friends, but all the while they gather gossip, and when they leave, they spread it everywhere.

**8** All who hate me whisper about me, imagining the worst.

**9** 'He has some fatal disease,' they say. 'He will never get out of that bed!'

**10** Even my best friend, the one I trusted completely, the one who shared my food, has turned against me.

**11** LORD, have mercy and raise me up, so I can pay them back!

**12** I know You are pleased with me, for my enemy does not triumph over me.

**13** You have preserved my life because I am innocent. You have brought me into Your presence forever.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **41:9**: The 'thing of Belial' (worthlessness/wickedness) — the enemies believe David is under a divine curse. Sickness is interpreted as divine judgment.

— PNEUMA
